implement.summary: Defect on BASE_SHA 42291369: apps/mobile/src/screens/ManageAccountScreen.tsx imported only the legacy two-call client (lines 52-53) and called requestAccountDeletion at line 458 and confirmAccountDeletion at line 492; apps/mobile/src/account/deletion.ts (266 lines) posted through a plain fetchFn (lines 135-136) with no redirect:'error'/credentials:'omit', no operation id, no status capability, no journal — so a lost confirmation could only be shown as an unrecoverable 'unknown' message, closing the dialog or restarting the app lost the attempt, and deletionOperation.ts/deletionOperationTransport.ts were unreferenced by any shipping source (pinned by deletionOperationIsolation.test.ts). Fix: deletion.ts gains fetchNoRedirect (forces redirect:'error', credentials:'omit', cache:'no-store', referrerPolicy:'no-referrer' and marks any reply whose url differs from the request or is missing as redirected), a production DeletionRuntimePort (origin snapshot from runtimeConfig, owner snapshot from accountScope, bearer resolved per request from the api session only when origin+owner match), a per-db cached foundation over the app's transactional SQLite db and the device Keychain (via new sessionVault.deviceKeychainForVault), durableAccountDeletionFlow(getDb)/legacyAccountDeletionFlow(client) behind one AccountDeletionFlow interface, and an AccountDeletionState union (ready | request_unknown | confirm_unknown | in_progress | failed{nothing_deleted|unknown} | completed). ManageAccountScreen now journals request → armed (5s countdown, never before the foundation's reviewAfterMs) → confirm → completed; a lost step-1 reply stays request_unknown and is retried under the same job ('Retry request'); a lost or 202 in-progress confirmation renders 'Deletion status unknown' / 'Deletion in progress' and is recovered/polled through the stored status capability, with 'Account deleted' + local cleanup reached only from a verified completion receipt (foundation seal) — the completed path still hands the frozen original-owner context to onDeleted even if the signed-in owner changed mid-flight; opening the dialog calls flow.resume so an unfinished owner-scoped operation is reused instead of minting a second delete-request; a server 'expired'/'blocked' status returns to review as 'Nothing was deleted' and re-enables a fresh request; owner/origin changes make the attempt stale (foundation fencing + the screen's owner re-check). The legacy client remains the fallback only when the db cannot host the journal (mocked db that throws / non-transactional). Survey bodies now pass through deletionOperation.request/retryRequest → transport.request → delete-request. Commits: e1d46d94 (regression test, fails 13/14 on base) and aa491505 (implementation). Pushed only devin/pp/w08-01/impl-r1; no PR, no main/ci/mac-* pushes, no production Supabase/App Store Connect actions.

non_blocking_issues: INFERRED (not runnable on Linux): fetchNoRedirect relies on RN's fetch honouring redirect:'error' OR on response.url differing from the request URL when the iOS networking stack follows a redirect. RN's whatwg-fetch polyfill sets Response.url from XHR responseURL, so a followed redirect is detected via the URL mismatch; a redirect back to the identical URL (pathological) would not be. Behaviour on-device is untested here — Mac runner verification remains authoritative for iOS runtime claims.

INFERRED: durableAccountDeletionFlow falls back silently to legacyAccountDeletionFlow when getDb() is non-transactional/owner-scoped or the Keychain module fails to load. Production getDb() returns the transactional db so the durable path is taken, but no diagnostic is emitted when the fallback is chosen (diagnostics transport is disabled by policy, so this is acceptable).

residual_risks: Linux-only evidence: Keychain and SQLite are exercised through the Jest mocks/in-memory DB; real iOS Keychain write-failure timing (A1) and same-frame double taps on device were not run on the M4 (not permitted for this package). Native behaviour remains INFERRED.

Journal reclamation is driven by the device clock (challenge expiresAt); a clock moved forward reclaims a never-confirmed row early (owner simply gets a fresh request), a clock moved backward delays reclamation until the server reports the operation expired/superseded via status. Receipts, unresolved confirmations and unknown requests are never reclaimed, so worst case is 'journal full' copy that is honest about it.

Capacity remains device-global (32 rows across owners). Live requests of other accounts are intentionally not reclaimed, so a device shared by >32 accounts each with a live (unexpired, unconfirmed) request cannot start a 33rd until one expires (15-minute challenge window); the copy states this instead of promising a retry.

The `while (inFlightRef.current) await …` in resumeUnfinished awaits an already-running step from a previous presentation before resuming; a step that never settles (hung fetch beyond the transport timeout) would delay resume until the transport timeout fires.
implement.summary: Defects on BASE_SHA (42291369): ManageAccountScreen.tsx still called the legacy requestAccountDeletion/confirmAccountDeletion client (plain fetch following redirects; no journal, no idempotent re-entry), and deletion.ts exported no fetchNoRedirect (base suite: 19/20 fail). Round-1 breaks reproduced on the r1 wiring and fixed: A1 — deletion.ts durableState mapped phase 'securing' with 'ready' (line ~604 on r1) and resume() treated only 'ready' as re-requestable, so a Keychain-write failure after the securing journal write showed 'Deletion status unknown … may have completed' for 24h; now securing is never confirmable, resume skips it and offers a fresh request, and capability-less securing rows are reclaimable. A3 — ManageAccountScreen.runStep had no synchronous in-flight guard, so a second same-frame press re-entered confirm() and the foundation's job lock ('stale_handler') was rendered as account-changed/unknown; now a second press is a no-op and the UI stays 'Deleting…' with exactly one /delete-confirm. A4 — deletionOperationJournal.create refused a 33rd row with journal_capacity and no code path ever removed rows; now journal.remove()/foundation.reclaim() free inert rows (server-closed, lapsed never-confirmed challenges, capability-less securing) and request() reclaims once before failing, with copy that no longer promises retrying will help when nothing could be freed. Bonus: a challenge the device clock says expired is not resumed/armed; confirming it fails honestly as nothing_deleted with a fresh request.
